newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end sharply down on rupiah, results.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end sharply down on rupiah, results.

text.p: Jakarta's share index fell sharply on Wednesday as investors sold stocks across the board on concern over the central bank's tight rupiah policy and poor first-half results of some blue chip companies, brokers said.
The composite index was down 14.02 points, or 1.96 percent, to close at 699.86 points after touching a day's low of 695.75 points. Decliners led advancers by 141 to 15 with 42 issues unchanged.
Trading volume, however, was modest with an estimated total market turn-over of 463 billion rupiah.

"Players sold stocks across the board, with property stocks suffering the heaviest blow, because of the central bank's tight rupiah policy which prompted banks to raise interest rates," one broker said.

Bank Indonesia's recent policy of increasing short-term rates of central bank certificates (SBIs) and staying out of the short-term securities market (SSBPUs) was aimed at reducing speculative attacks on the rupiah, the broker said.
The central bank's move, however, tightened rupiah liquidity, pushed up the rupiah interbank rate and prompted banks to increase interest rates, he said.
Brokers said property stocks were dealt the heaviest blow, with most stocks in the sector suffering losses.
Brokers said disappointment over the first half results of some blue chips such as Semen Gresik and Tambang Timah also weakened sentiment.
Semen Gresik fell 250 rupiah to touch a year's low of 6,300 rupiah, with some 2.1 million shares traded due to poor first half results, brokers said.
They said the market focus was on newly-listed Kyoei Steel, which was the most actively traded stock.
Kyoei managed to stage a modest debut despite overall weak market sentiment due partly to some support from its underwriters, one broker said.
Kyoei ended at 800 rupiah against an initial offer price of 650 rupiah. It opened at 800 rupiah and touched a high of 825 rupiah.
